data.title: Oil marketing companies reject Karnataka's claims of 26-31 pc ethanol in petrol, cite testing irregularities
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) have rejected claims by the Karnataka government that petrol sold at certain retail outlets in the state contains 26-31 per cent ethanol, as per a release by the OMCs.

The three OMCs asserted that E20 petrol supplied nationwide complies with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) specification IS 17021, rejecting the Karnataka government's claim that petrol sold at certain retail outlets in the state contains 26-31 per cent ethanol.

"The OMCs would like to clarify that the claims, as reported, are not supported by testing conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures. E20 petrol supplied by the three OMCs across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline," the release said.

The OMCs also raised concerns over the sampling procedure and testing methodology adopted during the October 2026 exercise, citing deviations from the prescribed norms under the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel Control Order, 2005, and Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024.

According to the OMCs, the prescribed procedure requires six one-litre samples, with two each provided to the dealer, retained by the oil company or department, and sent to a designated laboratory for testing.

While samples collected in September 2026 were tested at designated OMC laboratories, the October exercise reportedly took place without OMC representatives.

The companies said they had not received retention samples, outlet-wise details or laboratory reports despite requesting them.

The OMCs further questioned the reliance on certificates issued by a third-party laboratory instead of a laboratory specified under the Control Order, stating that the certificates lacked sufficient technical details to independently verify the reported ethanol content.

They added that the absence of retention samples and prescribed documentation prevented the companies and concerned dealers from seeking verification or retesting.

The OMCs further stated that under IS 17021:2018 (Amendment No. 3, August 2025), ethanol content in E20 petrol must be tested using prescribed methods, including Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), water extraction or Gas Chromatography.

They noted that Gas Chromatography testing under ASTM D4815/D6839 requires samples to be diluted with oxygenate-free petrol in a 1:1 ratio, with results corrected against an E10 certified reference material.

However, the laboratory certificates cited by the Karnataka government only mention "Ethanol % by Gas Chromatography", without specifying the testing standard, dilution procedure or reference material used.

"In the absence of these essential details, the reported ethanol figures of 26-31% cannot be independently validated against the methodology prescribed under IS 17021," the OMCs said.

OMCs have requested the Government of Karnataka to share the complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the test methodology adopted for the reported findings.

data.title: Suspicious prediction market activity seen before election poll release: NYT
data.description:
Suspicious prediction market bets were placed shortly before two recent New York Times/Siena political polls were released to the public, according to a report.

Vanderbilt University researchers said a Polymarket user bet almost $200,000 on Oct. 31 that Nebraska Senator Pete Ricketts would be re-elected. An hour later, a Times/Siena poll was released showing Ricketts in the lead.

A Friday New York Times report said while it was not clear if the user had access to inside information, they won more than $77,000.

The user also placed similar large bets on other markets, including Kalshi, the report said.

“There’s a series of circumstances here that it’s hard to write it off as a random occurrence,” said Brett Goldstein of the Vanderbilt Institute of National Security. It “requires further investigation.”

Polymarket said it had spotted the trades and was investigating. Kalshi declined comment.

Cointelegraph reported in April that a US Army soldier had been charged after making more than $400,000 by betting on a prediction market allegedly using nonpublic information tied to a US operation involving then Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.

In a statement, the Department of Justice alleged that Master Sergeant Gannon Ken Van Dyke was involved in the planning and execution of Operation Absolute Resolve, which led to the capture of Maduro at a residence in Caracas, Venezuela, in January.

Van Dyke allegedly used this information to buy “yes” shares in related Polymarket contracts, including “Maduro out by January 31” and “Trump invokes War Powers against Venezuela by January 31,” according to the DOJ.

data.title: Kirloskar-backed NBFC Arka gets Rs.525 cr initial commitment from TPG's Rise Funds
data.description:
Mumbai, Nov. 7 -- Arka Fincap Ltd, a Kirloskar Group-promoted NBFC, has signed definitive agreements with The Rise Funds, TPG's global impact investing platform, for an initial investment of Rs.525 crore, the company said in a statement on Saturday.

The investment could increase by another Rs.275 crore, subject to Arka meeting specified business milestones and obtaining regulatory approvals.

The investment will provide growth capital to support the evolution of the business through deepening its geographical reach and accelerating investments in technology and risk management capabilities. Avendus Capital acted as the exclusive financial advisor to Arka.

"Many of India's MSMEs and vehicle operators remain underserved by formal financial services, and Arka has built a disciplined, secured retail lending platform to serve these customers, with the potential to reach even more customers at scale," said Simit Batra, BU Partner, TPG.

With TPG's sector experience and innovative approach towards building and scaling successful financial institutions, combined with Kirloskar Group's long-term institutional commitment, deep understanding of the geography and the customer, Arka is well positioned to capitalize on the vast opportunity in India's secured lending market, the companies said in the statement.

"Crossing Rs.1,000 crore in secured retail assets is a defining milestone in our ambition to build a formidable, future-ready financial enterprise, serving entrepreneurial aspirations of our country," said Samrat Gupta, managing director of Arka.

TPG's investment marks a significant milestone in Arka's evolution into a diversified, secured retail lending institution. From its inception in 2018, the company has built a stable and sustainable business. Over the past 18 months, the company has strengthened its leadership, built a pan-regional distribution network, and incubated new secured lending businesses towards delivering value to all stakeholders.

With an AUM of about Rs.8,000 crore and a presence across ten states through 146 branches, Arka is building a broader and more granular lending franchise, while continuing to leverage its established wholesale lending platform.

The NBFC offers financing solutions spanning pre-owned vehicle financing, secured business loans, loan against property and wholesale lending. The company serves entrepreneurs, MSMEs, vehicle operators and corporate clients through a combination of specialised lending businesses and a growing distribution network.

TPG's impact platform manages about $37 billion in assets across a family of funds that pursue non-concessionary returns and social and environmental impact at scale through growth equity, private equity, and infrastructure investing strategies. The Rise Funds- a core pillar of its global impact investing platform delivers capabilities and expertise across a wide variety of sectors and countries at scale, focusing on opportunities in climate and decarbonization, education, financial inclusion, healthcare, and impact technology.

"As a group, we have always placed great value on enduring partnerships and the institution-building ethos of creating businesses that stand the test of time," said Gauri Kirloskar, vice chairperson and managing director, Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd (KOEL).

KOEL is one of the flagship companies of the Kirloskar Group, which has been in business for eight decades. It is one of the leading engineering and manufacturing companies and offers a energy and power solutions, including engines, generator sets, industrial engines, agricultural equipment, and water management solutions.

data.title: Voltas gets a new Chairman: Who is Sunil D'Souza, his career and education, and why is Noel Tata stepping down?
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Voltas Ltd is set for a leadership change, with Sunil Alaric D'Souza taking over as Chairman from November 12, 2026, following Noel Tata's retirement upon attaining the age of 70, in line with the Tata Group Governance Guidelines.

The company's board approved Noel Tata's retirement as Chairman and Director with effect from the close of business hours on November 11, 2026, at its meeting on November 6. He will take over as Chairman Emeritus from November 12, Voltas said in an exchange filing.

D'Souza, who is currently a Director on the Voltas board, will assume the chairmanship from the same date. He is also the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Tata Consumer Products.

Sunil Alaric D'Souza is the Managing Director and CEO of Tata Consumer Products, a position he has held since April 2020. He has more than three decades of experience in the consumer products industry, with a career spanning Hindustan Unilever, PepsiCo and Whirlpool India.

Before joining Tata Consumer Products, D'Souza served as Managing Director of Whirlpool India for more than four years. He played a major role in transforming the company's business in the country.

Earlier, he spent nearly 15 years at PepsiCo, where he held several leadership positions. His responsibilities included overseeing the commercial operations of the company's food and beverage portfolio and managing business operations across a large cluster of Asian countries.

D'Souza began his career with Hindustan Unilever in 1993. His professional experience spans business strategy, growth, commercial operations and execution across consumer-facing businesses.

D'Souza holds an engineering degree from the University of Madras and is an alumnus of the Indian Institute of Management, Calcutta (IIM-C).

His academic background in engineering and management, combined with his experience across major consumer goods companies, has shaped a career spanning manufacturing, business strategy and leadership roles.

Apart from leading Tata Consumer Products as its MD and CEO, D'Souza serves on the boards of several companies within the Tata Group and its associated businesses.

These include Voltas Ltd, Tata Digital Pvt Ltd, Tata Starbucks Ltd, Capital Foods Pvt Ltd, Organic India Pvt Ltd and several overseas subsidiaries of Tata Consumer Products.

His appointment as Voltas Chairman adds another leadership responsibility to his existing roles across the group.

Noel Tata's retirement from Voltas follows the Tata Group's governance guidelines, under which he is stepping down after attaining the age of 70.

He has been associated with Voltas since 2003. The company said his leadership, strategic guidance and contributions had helped shape its growth, strengthen its market position and create sustainable value.

His departure from the Voltas board is part of a broader transition across Tata Group companies. Noel Tata is also scheduled to retire from the boards of Trent and Titan in accordance with the group's governance guidelines.

Trent has announced his retirement as Chairman and Director with effect from the close of business hours on November 11, 2026, with his appointment as Chairman Emeritus from November 12. Titan has separately announced that he will retire as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director and Vice-Chairman with effect from November 12.

data.title: Kirloskar Oil Engines arm Arka Fincap signs ₹800 crore investment deal with TPG
data.description:
Kirloskar Oil Engines-backed Arka Fincap has signed definitive agreements with TPG's The Rise Funds for an investment of up to ₹800 crore across two tranches, as the non-banking financial company (NBFC) looks to accelerate its growth and expand its secured retail lending business.

The investment comprises an initial ₹525 crore, with the potential for an additional ₹275 crore through a subsequent tranche, subject to the achievement of specified business milestones and requisite regulatory approvals, Arka said in a statement on Saturday, November 7.

The capital infusion will support Arka's expansion into new geographies, while accelerating investments in technology and risk management capabilities. The partnership is aimed at building a scaled, diversified and secured retail-led financial institution.

Founded in 2018, Arka has built assets under management (AUM) of around ₹8,000 crore, including a secured retail portfolio of over ₹1,000 crore. It operates through 146 branches across 10 states and employs more than 2,000 people.

The company has also strengthened its leadership and expanded its distribution network over the past 18 months, while building new secured lending businesses alongside its established wholesale lending platform.

Gauri Kirloskar, Vice Chairperson and Managing Director of Kirloskar Oil Engines, said the partnership reflects the group's focus on long-term relationships and institution-building.

Arka Managing Director Samrat Gupta said crossing ₹1,000 crore in secured retail assets was a key milestone in the company's ambition to build a technology-led financial services business.

Simit Batra, Business Unit Partner at TPG, said Arka's secured retail lending platform offered an opportunity to serve underserved micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and vehicle operators with greater access to formal credit.

Arka is promoted by the Kirloskar Group through publicly listed Kirloskar Oil Engines and carries a CRISIL AA/Stable rating.

Avendus Capital acted as the exclusive financial advisor to Arka, while AZB & Partners advised the company on legal matters. Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas was TPG's legal advisor.

data.title: HCG Reports 16% Revenue Growth In Q2 FY27, Adjusted EBITDA Rises 17%
data.description:
Higher patient volumes, advanced oncology treatments and international business growth support the cancer hospital network's financial performance

Healthcare Global Enterprises Limited (HCG), India's largest dedicated cancer hospital network, reported a 15.8 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue from operations to Rs 7,318 million in Q2 FY2027, for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. Adjusted EBITDA rose 17.2 per cent to Rs 1,425 million, compared with Rs 1,215 million in the corresponding quarter last year, supported by higher patient volumes and improved revenue per patient.

For the first half of FY2027, revenue increased 14.6 per cent year-on-year to Rs 14,100 million, while adjusted EBITDA grew 18.3 per cent to Rs 2,740 million. EBITDA margin improved to 19.7 per cent, compared with 18.8 per cent in H1 FY2026.

Patient volumes increased 9 per cent during the quarter, while average revenue per patient (ARPP) grew 7 per cent, driven by a favourable payor mix and increased contributions from advanced oncology treatments. Robotic surgeries recorded 37 per cent year-on-year growth. International business revenue also increased approximately 54 per cent to Rs 302 million, supported by higher patient volumes in radiation and medical oncology.

Expansion And Clinical Innovation

Commenting on the performance, Dr Manish Mattoo, CEO of HCG, said the company recorded growth through improved revenue mix, higher contributions from complex oncology treatments and operational efficiencies. The non-institutional business contributed 69 per cent of revenue, an improvement of 325 basis points year-on-year.

During the quarter, HCG added 25 operational beds across Kenya, Kolkata and Nagpur, taking total bed additions to 146 in H1 FY2027. The network also operationalised an MR-LINAC adaptive radiation therapy system at North Bengaluru, a linear accelerator in Africa and a cardiac robotic surgery system at HMS Ahmedabad.

The company expanded its clinical capabilities by performing its first CAR-T cell therapy at HCC Ahmedabad. It also introduced robotic breast surgery, robotic spine surgery and Transoral Robotic Surgery (TORS) across selected facilities. In precision diagnostics, HCG launched a 1,212-gene liquid biopsy panel and introduced two nuclear medicine tracers at KR.

Dr B. S. Ajaikumar, Founder and Non-Executive Chairman of HCG, highlighted the company's research focus on multi-omics, organoid technology, cellular therapies, including CAR-T, and longevity research. The company said its priorities include improving asset utilisation, ramping up newer facilities, expanding capacity and increasing access to advanced cancer care.

data.title: Sigma Advanced Systems Reports Rs 417 Cr Q2 Revenue, Pat Rises To Rs 48.6 Cr
data.description:
Sigma Advanced Systems reported consolidated operational revenue of Rs 417.07 crore for the second quarter of FY27, registering an 11.43 per cent increase over the previous quarter, as acquisitions, aerospace and defence orders and expanded manufacturing operations supported its growth.

The company reported a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 48.60 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, up 37.24 per cent from Rs 35.41 crore in the first quarter of FY27.

Consolidated operational EBITDA stood at Rs 82.28 crore, compared with Rs 61 crore in the preceding quarter, marking a 35.06 per cent increase. The EBITDA margin was 19.73 per cent, while the gross margin stood at 66.32 per cent.

For the first half of FY27, Sigma reported consolidated operational revenue of Rs 791.34 crore, operational EBITDA of Rs 143.20 crore and PAT of Rs 84.01 crore. The company said the half-year performance was not directly comparable with the corresponding period of the previous year because of changes in its business composition and expansion in the scale of operations during FY26.

Acquisition Strengthens Aerospace Business

During the quarter, Sigma completed the acquisition of 100 per cent of UK-based Bromford Precision Solutions Limited for an enterprise value of approximately GBP 11.89 million, or around Rs 153 crore.

Based in Leicester, Bromford manufactures high-precision aero-engine rings and other engine structures. The acquisition has strengthened Sigma's position in the global aerospace supply chain, particularly its relationship with Rolls-Royce.

Within weeks of the acquisition, Bromford secured another long-term agreement with Rolls-Royce valued at nearly GBP 125 million, or approximately Rs 1,600 crore. This is in addition to a GBP 300 million agreement signed in April 2026. The two agreements together are valued at nearly GBP 425 million, equivalent to around Rs 5,400 crore.

Sigma also said its Sri City manufacturing facility had commenced operations following the transfer of work from its UK operations. The facility has produced and delivered its first batch of aerospace components to Nasmyth's UK customers, marking a step in the company's India-UK manufacturing integration strategy.

Its UK subsidiary, Nasmyth, also received the Innovation Award at the 2026 Global Boeing Supplier Summit in Seattle for its research and development work.

Rs 3,915 Crore In New Orders Since July

Sigma said it had secured new orders and long-term agreements worth approximately Rs 3,915 crore since July 2026 across its aerospace and defence businesses.

The orders include a USD 104.9 million export contract, valued at approximately Rs 1,013 crore, from a North American customer for the manufacture and supply of 155 mm base-bleed artillery shell bodies. The order is scheduled for execution over six to 12 months.

In October, the company secured a USD 19.7 million order, worth around Rs 174 crore, from a North American NATO customer for 155 mm artillery ammunition subsystems, with execution scheduled by the second quarter of 2027.

It also won a USD 102.23 million contract, valued at approximately Rs 973.64 crore, from a NATO customer for the supply of base bleed units. The order is to be executed over 12 months.

In the counter-drone segment, Sigma and Indrajaal Autonomous Defense Systems secured orders worth approximately Rs 155 crore from the Government of India for the Indrajaal Ranger anti-drone patrol vehicle.

The company also signed an exclusive memorandum of understanding with Munitions India Limited on 14 October for the integration, indigenous manufacturing and supply of 155 mm artillery course correction fuses.

To support its expansion plans, Sigma completed a preferential allotment of Rs 460 crore in August at Rs 347 per share, with participation from mutual funds and other investors.

Commenting on the results, Sunil Kalidindi, CEO and Executive Director of Sigma Advanced Systems, said the Bromford acquisition and the second Rolls-Royce agreement had strengthened the company's position with global aerospace manufacturers. He added that the operational Sri City facility and recent ammunition orders provided a stronger foundation for growth in the second half of FY27.

data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Hindalco Industries shares are in focus after the company reported a strong set of results for the September quarter of FY27, with consolidated net profit rising nearly 59% year-on-year. The stock closed 1.88% higher at Rs.957.70 apiece on the BSE on Friday.

The stock has gained 7.25% over the past week and 11.30% in the last two weeks. It has risen 1.89% over the past month and 21.53% over the past year. However, Hindalco shares remain down 6.71% over three months and 8.47% over six months. The stock has gained 7.01% year-to-date.

Hindalco Industries reported a 58.8% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to Rs.7,533 crore in the September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs.4,741 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Consolidated income rose to Rs.92,651 crore from Rs.66,771 crore in the year-ago period, the Aditya Birla Group company said in a regulatory filing.

The company's EBITDA for the quarter increased 42% year-on-year to Rs.13,757 crore, reflecting strong contributions across its business segments.

In a statement, Hindalco said the record performance was underpinned by the strength of its integrated business model, led by a solid primary upstream business and complemented by strong contributions from its downstream operations.

The company's copper business recorded its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA, while subsidiary Novelis sustained its improved performance, supported by the normalisation of operations at its Oswego facility.

Hindalco's India aluminium production costs are expected to remain elevated in the December quarter, with coal costs likely to keep input expenses under pressure.

Speaking at a media briefing, managing director Satish Pai said production costs for the company's India aluminium business could be around 5% higher in Q3 compared with Q2. However, costs are expected to start moderating in the March quarter as coal availability improves.

"Q3 will be 5% above Q2. By Q4, costs should start coming down because coal availability in the northern region should improve once winter sets in and power demand in the northern areas declines," Pai said.

He added that coal prices in northern India remained elevated in October, keeping input costs high for the company's smelters in the near term.

Pai also highlighted continued tightness in domestic coal supplies, noting that inventories at some of the company's plants were at around 50% of normal levels. In contrast, coal inventories at its Odisha facilities remained at normal levels.

The company expects the cost pressures to ease in Q4 as coal availability improves with the onset of winter and power demand moderates in northern India.

Hindalco said its non-LME-linked businesses contributed nearly 50% of its earnings, highlighting the growing importance of these operations in supporting performance amid volatility in London Metal Exchange (LME) prices and global macroeconomic uncertainty.

The company expects upcoming projects, including the commissioning and ramp-up of Bay Minette, copper recycling, aluminium battery foil, Aditya flat-rolled products (FRP), and Inner Grooved Tubes, to further increase the contribution from its non-LME-linked businesses.

On the upstream front, Hindalco's aluminium refinery and smelter projects, copper smelters and coal mine developments remain on track, the company said.

These investments aim to strengthen its integrated business model by combining upstream capabilities with downstream expansion to support long-term growth across market cycles.

Nuvama Institutional Equities said Hindalco has hedged 26% of its estimated FY28 aluminium volumes at $3,168 per tonne, providing a cushion against potential downside in aluminium prices. The brokerage noted that this would help limit earnings risks, factoring in its LME aluminium price assumptions of $3,000 per tonne for FY28 and $2,700 per tonne for FY29.

It expects Novelis' earnings and cash flows to improve from Q4FY27 onwards. Nuvama has raised its FY27 and FY28 EBITDA estimates by 4-5%, factoring in higher copper profits. The brokerage upgraded the stock to 'BUY' from its earlier rating and raised its target price to Rs.1,184 from Rs.1,108. At the revised target, Hindalco trades at 5.6 times its FY28 estimated EV/EBITDA.

data.title: Peter Schiff Predicts Gold Boom, Says Political Shift Threatens To Send Inflation Soaring — ‘Sign Of Things To Come’
data.description:
Key points:
  • With major U.S. stock market indexes ending the week lower, gold mining stocks stood out as one of the market's strongest performers.
  • Schiff highlighted the surge in the VanEck Gold Miners ETF over the past week, arguing that the gains could be a precursor to a broader rally in gold.
  • Higher inflation has historically strengthened gold's appeal among investors seeking protection against declining purchasing power.

Gold mining stocks emerged as a rare bright spot during a difficult week for equities, drawing attention from longtime gold bull Peter Schiff. The economist sees the rally as a potential signal of a much bigger move ahead for precious metals.

In a post on X, Schiff argued that a political shift to the left could fuel higher inflation, creating an especially favorable environment for gold. He pointed to the latest gains in gold mining stocks as an early indication of what's coming.

Gold Miners Surge, Schiff Sees Inflation-Driven Rally Ahead

With major U.S. stock market indexes ending the week lower, gold mining stocks stood out as one of the market's strongest performers.

Schiff highlighted the surge in the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) over the past week, arguing that the gains could be a precursor to a broader rally in gold.

“This is a sign of things to come. A sharp turn to the left, and the higher inflation that will result, will be extremely bullish for gold,” he said.

He argued about the prospect of a shift in political priorities leading to policies that put additional upward pressure on prices. Higher inflation has historically strengthened gold's appeal among investors seeking protection against declining purchasing power.

However, the latest move in gold miners comes against a backdrop of considerable volatility in the underlying metal.

Shares of gold miners Newmont Corp. (NEM), Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd. (AEM), Barrick Mining Corp. (B), and Franco-Nevada Corp. (FNV) soared between 10% and 16% this week.

Gold Rebounds From One-Year Low, But ING Sees Challenges Ahead

Spot gold prices recovered this week after three weeks of decline, with the yellow metal registering its best week since August.

According to analysts at ING Think, the rebound was supported by bargain hunting and a pullback in oil prices as signs of easing U.S.-Iran tensions helped ease some inflation concerns that had weighed on the metal.

However, the firm cautioned that gold's recovery could face obstacles in the near term. The precious metal has been caught in a broader risk-off move alongside heavy selling in technology stocks, while expectations of higher interest rates and a stronger U.S. dollar have weighed on investor sentiment.

The firm expects gold to regain some ground following its recent correction but sees limited scope for a sustained recovery while those headwinds persist.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 0.17%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) rose 0.21%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged up by 0.06%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: Crusoe Completes Wyoming AI Data Center Development, Sells Site To Google
data.description:
OTTAWA (dpa-AFX) - Crusoe, an AI infrastructure and data center developer, said Google has acquired its data center site in southeast Wyoming, completing Crusoe's role in the project's early-stage development and advancing Google's expansion of AI and cloud infrastructure in the region.

The transaction marks the culmination of Crusoe's pre-development work for the Wyoming campus, which included site selection, securing governmental approvals, and developing a power strategy for the project. Financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.

Crusoe and Tallgrass Energy jointly initiated the Wyoming campus by developing both power and data center infrastructure in parallel. The effort involved coordinating energy system design, data center engineering, site development, and engagement with hyperscale customers to prepare the site for large-scale deployment.

The sale highlights Crusoe's strategy of developing AI-ready infrastructure projects and transitioning them to major technology companies. The company recently disclosed that it is serving as the developer for Google's data center campus currently under construction in Armstrong County near Amarillo, Texas.

The Wyoming acquisition further strengthens Google's data center footprint as demand for computing capacity accelerates amid growing artificial intelligence workloads, while allowing Crusoe to focus on advancing additional AI infrastructure developments.

data.title: Muhurat Trading Strategy Diwali Day 2026: What to do, what to buy, what to avoid? Trading guide for Nov 8 - Key levels
data.description:
Muhurat Trading 2026, Nov. 7 -- The Indian stock market will open for its annual Muhurat trading session on Sunday, November 8, marking the beginning of Samvat 2083. The special Diwali session is considered an auspicious occasion to start investing and review financial goals. However, investors should not let the festive sentiment drive impulsive decisions.

With limited liquidity during the session and benchmark indices nearing important resistance levels, analysts recommend a cautious, stock-specific approach. While long-term investors can use the occasion to review their portfolios and make selective investments, short-term traders should watch key technical levels, track global cues and avoid aggressive positions.

Analysts believe Muhurat trading offers investors an opportunity to review their asset allocation, assess whether their portfolios are aligned with their financial goals and rebalance where necessary. They favour a stock-specific approach to long-term investing, while advising caution during the short trading window.

Liquidity is typically limited during the special session, making it inadvisable to place large orders or undertake aggressive buying and selling. New investors can consider token investments in fundamentally strong companies they are interested in holding for the long term. Investors should avoid buying stocks merely because it is an auspicious occasion and instead focus on valuations, business fundamentals and their investment objectives.

Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOSL) said Nifty valuations were attractive at 17.5 times forward earnings, 16% below the long-term average. However, it noted that small-cap stocks continued to trade at a 25% premium to their long-term average, warranting selectivity.

"We perceive FY27 to mark a return to double-digit earnings growth, with Nifty EPS expected to grow 16%/14% YoY in FY27/FY28 vs 5% in FY26. Nifty valuations are attractive at 17.5x forward earnings, 16% below the long-term average," MOSL said.

For Samvat 2083, MOSL favours banking and financial services, capital markets, manufacturing, global outsourcing and exports, consumption and digital businesses. It sees opportunities in healthcare devices, aerospace, auto components, pharmaceutical ingredients, garments, port cargo, organised jewellery and quick-commerce platforms.

The market's technical setup will be important during Sunday's Muhurat trading session, with both benchmark indices approaching resistance zones after a recent rally. Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking, expects a sideways-to-consolidative session and has identified immediate support and resistance levels for Nifty and Bank Nifty. Traders will also need to track geopolitical developments, crude oil prices and global market cues before taking positions.

"For Muhurat trading, the overall market bias is likely to remain sideways to consolidative after the recent sharp upside move, as both benchmark indices are approaching crucial resistance zones. Nifty is trading around 24,600," Tailor said.

Tailor identified immediate support for Nifty at 24,350 and resistance in the 24,700-24,800 range, where rejection was visible. He cautioned that profit booking could emerge after six consecutive sessions of gains, particularly amid geopolitical concerns, crude oil volatility and the global market sell-off seen in US markets on November 5 and early Asian trading on November 6.

For Bank Nifty, the 57,500-57,800 range is important, with stronger resistance at 58,000-58,400 and support around 56,000-56,300. The support zone coincides with the index's 200-day exponential moving average and a previous trendline breakout area.

Tailor advised traders to monitor global cues and geopolitical developments and wait for a clear directional move instead of taking aggressive positions. Long-term investors, meanwhile, can use technical retracements to accumulate fundamentally strong stocks at lower levels with a longer-term perspective.

Meanwhile, Sumeet Bagadia placed Nifty 50's immediate support at 24,800-24,850 and resistance at 25,130-25,200 at the beginning of Samvat 2083.

data.title: WULF Stock Rebounds From Lowest Close In Over A Year, B. Riley Says Selloff ‘In No Way’ Justified
data.description:
Key points:
  • B. Riley analyst Nick Giles reiterated a 'Buy' rating on TeraWulf.
  • He called it one of the highest-quality names in its high-performance computing coverage.
  • The company’s third-quarter revenue jumped over 51% year-over-year to $76.2 million.

TeraWulf (WULF) shares rebounded from their lowest point in over a year on Friday, after the company reported its third-quarter results, with B.Riley saying the recent selloff was “in no way” justified for the stock.

The stock ended Friday’s session at around $11, while on Thursday, it closed at $10 before briefly dipping to $9, its lowest price in more than a year. Despite Friday’s gain, shares were still down over 3% for the week.

WULF stock closed up over 12% on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around WULF improved to the ‘bullish’ zone from ‘neutral,’ accompanied by ‘high’ chatter levels over the past day.

Why B.Riley Is Betting Big On WULF Stock

According to TheFly, B. Riley analyst Nick Giles reiterated a ‘Buy’ rating on the stock, adding that the company's HPC lease income nearly doubled from the prior quarter. Giles added that the recent selloff in shares was "in no way" justified for the stock.

Giles said the “next major catalyst” will be when the financing for TeraWulf’s Anthropic (ANT) lease is secured. He called the company “one of the highest-quality names in our HPC coverage.” The deal would help ease the concerns about funding and dilution that have been hanging over the stock, Giles said.

The 20-year lease covered roughly 401 megawatts of computing power at TeraWulf's Justified campus and is expected to generate about $19 billion during its first term.

The company announced on Tuesday that Alphabet Inc.’s (GOOG, GOOGL) Google was set to provide a credit backdrop to the firm. TeraWulf expects the first parts of the campus to be ready by the end of 2027 and the rest to follow in the second quarter of 2028.

Data Center Leases Drive Revenue

TeraWulf reported third-quarter revenue of $76.2 million, about 51% higher than $50.6 million a year ago. The company's revenue was 19% above analyst expectations of $64.07 million, according to Koyfin.

Most of that revenue came from leasing data-center space for high-performance computing, with its HPC lease income rising to $63 million, up from $7.2 million a year earlier. Bitcoin (BTC) mining revenue dropped to $13.2 million from $43.4 million.

Net income stood at $709.9 million, with most of it driven by a non-cash gain of $728.4 million. That gain stems from changes in the valuation of the company's warrant and derivative liabilities, the company said.

The company reported an adjusted loss of $0.03 per share, compared with the $0.38 loss that analysts expected, according to Koyfin data.

data.title: NSE's Electronic Gold Receipts record over ₹23 crore turnover on debut: How investors can buy
data.description:
Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs) worth approximately ₹23.34 crore changed hands on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on November 6, as trading in the segment backed by gold infrastructure company Augmont Enterprises witnessed activity on its opening day.

According to data shared by Augmont, 1,60,357 EGR units were traded by around 4:25 pm on Friday (November 6). The company said the segment saw active buying and selling, with prices moving in a range of ₹1,450.50 to ₹1,460 during the session. The bid-ask spread remained between ₹0.50 and ₹1.

The trading activity follows the collaboration between NSE and Augmont to develop the EGR ecosystem, which allows investors to hold and trade receipts representing ownership of physical gold through a demat account.

What are Electronic Gold Receipts?

EGRs are exchange-traded securities backed by physical gold stored in regulated vaults. They allow investors to buy and sell gold through the stock exchange without having to physically store the metal themselves.

The receipts are held in dematerialised form, like shares, and can be traded through a stockbroker. NSE offers EGR contracts in different denominations, including 100 milligrams, 1 gram, 10 grams, 100 grams and 1 kg, subject to the applicable product specifications.

The gold backing the receipts is stored with registered vault managers. Investors can continue holding the EGRs in their demat accounts or opt for physical delivery by following the prescribed withdrawal process. Physical withdrawal may involve additional charges, including storage, testing and transportation costs.

EGR trades follow a T+1 settlement cycle, meaning the securities and funds are transferred on the next working day after the trade.

How can investors buy EGRs?

Investors need an active trading and demat account with a stockbroker that offers access to the NSE's EGR segment. They can then place buy and sell orders through the broker's trading platform, similar to transactions in listed shares.

However, EGR trading is not necessarily available through every stockbroking platform. Investors should check with their existing broker whether it has enabled the EGR segment before attempting to place an order.

For instance, Zerodha's support page currently says that it does not support EGR trading, although the facility is expected to be enabled. This highlights the limited availability of the product across brokerage platforms.

What should investors check before buying?

Apart from the prevailing market price, investors should check the denomination and purity of the EGR contract, brokerage and depository charges, and any applicable vault storage charges.

Those considering physical delivery should also check the withdrawal process, minimum delivery quantity and associated charges with the relevant vault manager.

While EGRs provide an exchange-based route to hold gold, investors should also consider liquidity and the availability of buyers and sellers before placing orders.

data.title: Delhi HC says entire book cannot be stopped over few disputed passages; modifies restraint on 'Yes Man'
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Drawing a distinction between restraining specific allegedly defamatory material and stopping an entire published work, the Delhi High Court has held that a pre-trial injunction against a book cannot extend beyond the passages found, at the interim stage, to warrant such protection.

In a significant ruling for authors and publishers, the High Court modified a blanket restraint imposed on "Yes Man: The Untold Story of Rana Kapoor", authored by Pavan Chand Lall and published by HarperCollins, allowing the remaining portions of the book to remain outside the scope of the injunction.

Justice Harish Vaidyanathan Shankar held that the restraint would operate only against four specific passages identified in the trial court's order and not against the book in its entirety.

The Court found no reason, at the interim stage, to interfere with the trial court's findings concerning three statements held to be prima facie defamatory and one statement characterised as derogatory. However, it ruled that these findings could not form the basis for restraining the publication, sale, distribution and circulation of the entire literary work.

The ruling assumes significance for the scope of interim restrictions on books and other published material, particularly before a court has conducted a full trial on allegations of defamation.

The High Court stressed that an interlocutory injunction affecting publication should be confined to what is necessary to address the specific injury found at the interim stage.

The Court noted that the trial court had examined several statements challenged by former Yes Bank co-founder Rana Kapoor but had not found all of them to be defamatory. Only three statements were held to be prima facie defamatory, while one was characterised as derogatory.

Despite this, the operative direction had restrained the book as a whole. The High Court held that such a broad consequence could not be sustained.

"The remaining contents of the Subject Book have not been found, at this stage, to constitute defamatory or derogatory material," the Court noted while concluding that the restraint should remain confined to the four passages in question.

It said the narrower restraint would protect Kapoor against further dissemination of the specific imputations found prima facie objectionable without imposing an unnecessary restriction on the rest of the book.

Justice Shankar also underlined that findings recorded while considering interim relief are provisional and cannot be treated as a final adjudication of the dispute.

The Court clarified that the issues of truth, justification, fair comment, privilege and other defences would have to be examined at trial after a fuller adjudication.

The judgment, therefore, does not finally determine whether the allegations made in the disputed passages are true or false, nor does it amount to a final verdict on author Pavan Chand Lall's research, sources or defence to the defamation claim.

The Court further emphasised that an interlocutory injunction is intended to prevent apprehended injury during the pendency of proceedings and not to grant relief wider than the injury which has been found sufficient to warrant protection.

The dispute relates to "Yes Man: The Untold Story of Rana Kapoor", which examines the life and career of Kapoor in the context of the rise and subsequent crisis of Yes Bank.

The book was published on December 22, 2020 and had remained in circulation for a considerable period before the trial court passed its injunction on July 10, 2024.

The High Court recorded that the affairs of Yes Bank and Kapoor's role had attracted extensive public scrutiny, particularly after proceedings were initiated by the Enforcement Directorate and the Central Bureau of Investigation in March 2020. The developments had also received substantial coverage in print and electronic media.

The wider subject matter of the book was among the circumstances relevant to the Court's consideration of restrictions on its publication.

The judgment also reflects judicial caution regarding restraints imposed before a full trial, particularly where such orders affect literary works already in the public domain.

The High Court said an injunction operating upon publication ought to be no wider than necessary, and courts must remain conscious that interim findings are provisional.

It ultimately held that protecting a person's reputation against specific imputations found prima facie objectionable could be achieved without withdrawing an entire book from circulation.

The High Court accordingly modified the July 2024 order to provide that the injunction would apply only to the portions containing Statements (ii), (iv), (vii) and (x), as identified by the trial court.

The remaining portions of the book would not be covered by the injunction merely because of the findings concerning those four statements.

The Court clarified that its observations were confined to the scope of interim relief and should not be construed as a final expression of opinion on the merits of the allegations or the defences available to the parties.

The trial court will now proceed to adjudicate the defamation suit on its merits, uninfluenced by the High Court's observations except to the extent expressly determined for deciding the interim relief.
